text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen warned in a speech that a Danish "no" to the European Union's Amsterdam Treaty reforms would cost Denmark dearly, casting the country and the bloc into chaos with no prospect of any renegotiation. Denmark is to hold a referendum on the Amsterdam Treaty next year, with the latest opinion polls showing the narrowest of leads for supporters.

--Danish short haul air carrier Sun-Air of Scandinavia , which has a British Airways Express franchise, is to give up competition with SAS (Scandinavian Airles) on Danish domestic routes, accusing SAS of operating a monopoly.

--Some 16-18 percent of undecided Danish voters will have to vote for the lifting of Denmark's four opt-outs to the Maastricht Treaty if the solid 50 percent majority for preserving them is to be toppled, according to a Greens opinion poll. In 1993 Danes voted for Maastricht on condition that Denmark be excluded from single European currency, common defence and cross-border policy and legal cooperation.

--A pay boom with salary increases far in excess of those in trading partner nations is threatening Denmark's economic upturn, according to the Danish Employers' Federation, which urges the government to think of the business sector's needs in its 1998 state budget due for release in late August.
--Danes are making more and more overseas telephone calls as charges fall due to escalating competition.
--Denmark's pension funds are among the worst in Europe, according to a new EU survey.
